title: Sort before taking a few rows
summary: ORDER BY chooses the result order. LIMIT then restricts how many of those rows are returned.
introduction: ORDER BY chooses the result order. LIMIT then restricts how many of those rows are returned. Your task: Ask for the two longest books instead.
learningObjectives: Ask for the two longest books instead.
Explain the example for sort before taking a few rows

blocks.text: ORDER BY chooses the result order. LIMIT then restricts how many of those rows are returned.
Use PostgreSQL in a new practice database through psql or a database editor. These are PostgreSQL examples, not SQLite. They do not run in this site's SQL playground. Use only sample data.

blocks.code:
WITH books(title,pages) AS (VALUES ('Moon Trip',60),('Garden Days',40),('Tiny Seed',20))
SELECT title,pages FROM books ORDER BY pages,title LIMIT 2;
blocks.title: Sort before taking a few rows

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `ORDER BY` chooses a result order. Include a tie-break field when equal values need a stable order.
`SELECT` names the output values. `AS` can give a calculated result a readable column name.

blocks.text: Tiny Seed appears first, then Garden Days.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Without ORDER BY, the database does not promise which rows a LIMIT query returns first.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Ask for the two longest books instead.
